html:
October 7, 2026

Trump draws bipartisan backlash for saying Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews, @carolinegleich, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy, @aaronparnas

At a campaign rally in Nebraska, President Trump said of the war with Iran, "Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego," calling it "a very small price to pay" that would be "over with very soon," and the crowd reacted approvingly. California Governor Gavin Newsom called him "deranged and dangerous," Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said the remarks could compromise the city's safety, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said "we are not expendable," and Republican congressional candidate Jim Desmond, a Navy veteran, said no American city is an acceptable cost of war. Senator Alex Padilla noted at least 19 servicemembers have died in the unauthorized war with Iran. The White House disputed that reading, with spokesman Steven Cheung saying Trump meant U.S. cities would have been threatened had a nuclear-armed Iran not been stopped. Criticism continued for days afterward, with members of Congress, governors and some of his own supporters describing him as mentally unfit.

Administration bars international election monitors as Trump promises a 'midterm surprise'

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

For the first time in more than two decades, the Trump administration is refusing entry to international election observers from the OSCE, a posture otherwise shared only by Russia and Belarus; OSCE monitors were present for the 2018 midterms. The Justice Department is instead preparing to deploy more than a thousand of its own poll monitors. Trump has separately told supporters to "watch for the midterm surprise" without explaining what he means, and said Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought, a chief architect of Project 2025, would be one of the most important people in the country's history over the next few weeks. Commentators have urged voters to use nonpartisan election protection resources ahead of the November 3 vote.

Revised congressional report nearly doubles count of US aircraft lost or damaged in Iran war

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A revised congressional report now counts 81 U.S. aircraft lost or damaged in operations against Iran, up from 42 in May. The total includes both manned aircraft and drones that were damaged as well as those destroyed.

CENTCOM says US forces destroyed 13 commercial vessels enforcing Iran blockade

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

U.S. Central Command said American forces have destroyed 13 commercial vessels, disabled three more and redirected 130 while enforcing the blockade of Iran. The 13 destroyed vessels were struck over the past 12 weeks and were either violating the blockade or linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' shadow shipping network, according to CENTCOM.

Pentagon warned in 2025 that Houthi campaign could drain US munitions stocks

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Pentagon officials reportedly warned in early 2025 that a prolonged campaign against the Houthis could strain key U.S. munitions stockpiles. The warning preceded Operation Rough Rider and the far larger war with Iran, which has since heavily depleted several U.S. missile inventories.

Republican senators press Hegseth over Pentagon reorganization and cuts

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican senators are demanding more information and transparency about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's reorganization of the Pentagon and his proposed cuts to certain military positions. The pressure comes amid broader turmoil inside the Department of Defense while the United States continues to wage war overseas, with concern reported to extend to Trump himself.

Investigation finds 506 US citizens detained by federal immigration agents since 2025

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A new investigation documents 506 U.S. citizens detained by federal immigration agents since January 2025, including more than 70 children and teenagers. The Department of Homeland Security says its operations are targeted and that people who obstruct agents can be arrested.

Trump urges Republicans to vote by mail after years of attacking the practice

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

President Trump urged Republicans to vote early, by mail or in person in the November 3 midterms, saying in a video posted Saturday, "Vote early, vote by mail, or vote in person on Election Day." The appeal reverses years of claims that mail ballots are insecure and "inherently corrupt," though election officials and court reviews have found no evidence of widespread mail-voting fraud. The shift follows a September Supreme Court ruling striking down administration restrictions on mail ballots. About one-third of ballots in the 2024 presidential election were cast by mail, according to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission.

French school protests enter third week with 1,800 high schools blockaded

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

Students, teachers and parents marched across France on Tuesday as protests over teacher shortages, aging school buildings and school-day conditions entered a third week, with the High School Students Union reporting 1,800 high schools blockaded or closed. The government has deployed riot police as clashes spread; authorities say 6,100 people, mostly minors, have been arrested, while at least 715 police officers and 215 teenagers have been injured, and a 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police dispersal grenade. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu ordered ministers to address teacher absences, school hours, lunch breaks and building repairs by the end of October. The demands come as France faces rising borrowing costs, with 10-year bond yields briefly topping 5%, a 24-year high.

Support for Medicare-for-all reaches record 66% in KFF poll

tags: health, politics
sources: @groundnews

A record 66% of U.S. adults support Medicare-for-all, up from 53% in 2020, according to a KFF poll released Tuesday. Support included 84% of Democrats and 72% of independents, while 66% of Republicans opposed it. Backing fell to 52% when respondents were told a single-payer system would eliminate private insurance, and also declined when they heard arguments about higher taxes or treatment delays. Health care costs ranked as the top economic concern, with 60% worried about affording care; the September survey included 1,328 adults.

State of emergency declared as Tropical Storm Isaiah strengthens in the Gulf

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas

Tropical Depression 9 formed in the Gulf of Mexico and has strengthened into Tropical Storm Isaiah, prompting a state of emergency for parts of the Florida Panhandle. Forecasters expect it to become the first hurricane to make landfall in the United States this year, potentially as a category two storm, somewhere between eastern Louisiana and the Florida Panhandle. Landfall is expected between Friday and Saturday, with Mississippi and Alabama also in the projected path.

Army grounds roughly 400 Apache helicopters over transmission concerns

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army has grounded about 400 AH-64E Apaches, more than half its Apache fleet, over concerns with the aircraft's transmission. Officials say inspections and corrective work could take months. It is the second safety-related Apache stand-down in less than two months, following an August crash near Fort Hood that killed two soldiers.

Army sets December 3 firing-squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army has scheduled the execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad for December 3 at Fort Hood. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 shooting there. If carried out, it would be the first U.S. military execution since 1961, though federal court challenges could still delay it.

US troops on Okinawa restricted after Marine arrested on murder suspicion

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Nearly 30,000 U.S. troops on Okinawa face new restrictions after a Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbery and murder. For 48 hours there is no off-base liberty and no alcohol on or off base. That is followed by a 30-day period with a midnight-to-5 a.m. curfew and increased supervision at base gates.

Navy cuts reenlistment bonuses across hundreds of specialties

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Navy reenlistment bonus changes take effect October 8, with 212 bonus levels reduced and 16 eliminated under the fiscal 2027 plan. Some specialties gain bonuses, but for affected sailors the last effective reenlistment date under the previous rates is October 7.

Paramount Skydance closes $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery takeover

tags: markets, media
sources: @groundnews

Paramount Skydance completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, forming a combined company called Skydance led by CEO David Ellison and bringing Paramount, Warner Bros., CBS, CNN, HBO Max and Paramount+ under one owner. The deal cleared its final legal barriers after settlements with a coalition of U.S. states and a Hollywood writers union, and shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "SKYD." Former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz will serve as co-CEO and oversee integration. The company plans $6 billion in cost savings while managing about $80 billion in debt.

Hackers claim theft of data on more than 3,600 Trump Mobile customers

tags: privacy, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

A hacking group calling itself BYOD has claimed responsibility for stealing the personal data of more than 3,600 Trump Mobile customers, according to Straight Arrow News. The stolen information is said to include names, addresses, email addresses and phone numbers. Trump Mobile allegedly told the group it had "no team to handle this."

UK prosecutors detail new indecent image allegations against Andrew Tate

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Court documents filed by UK prosecutors and obtained by TMZ allege that Andrew Tate possessed extreme explicit imagery, including material involving animals, found on a laptop in his possession on or before July 18, 2015. Prosecutors also allege that one video showed Tate with a girl believed to be 17 and that messages indicated he knew she was underage, and that he held 66 indecent images of a child classified as category A under UK law. The Tates remain in a federal detention facility in Miami while fighting extradition, deny all allegations, and their lawyer has disputed the reports.

Colorado Republican governor candidate says he would again slam wife into door

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Victor Marx, a Republican candidate for governor of Colorado, told participants on a Zoom call that he does not regret slamming his wife into a door to teach her a lesson about self-defense and said, "I would do it again." He claimed she "fake cried" during the incident and described physicality as part of the nature of their relationship.

Cornell students stage campus-wide economic blackout over handling of assault case

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Cornell Black Students United and the Cornell NAACP organized a sit-in at the Toni Morrison Dining Hall titled "Zero Day," calling on students to skip classes and spend no money on campus. Organizers say the action is intended to pressure the administration and show solidarity with the Jane Doe in a sexual assault case involving fraternity members. Participants were asked to avoid dining halls, the campus store and all other university spending for the day.

Megyn Kelly criticized over remarks about fraternity assault accuser

tags: media
sources: @aaronparnas

Commentator Megyn Kelly was condemned after a transcript of her show circulated in which she questioned the account of the Jane Doe who says she was assaulted by fraternity members, suggesting she may have consented and commenting on her appearance. Kelly also questioned the timing of the woman coming forward and her decision to drink and attend a fraternity house. The remarks drew criticism given the size of her audience.

Naked Trump statue goes on display in European Parliament building

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

A statue depicting the U.S. president nude, holding a gold golf club and seated on the shoulders of a smaller figure, has gone on display inside the European Parliament building in Strasbourg, France. Titled "Orange Plague," it was created by Danish artists. Republicans have reacted angrily to the installation.

Claims link Israeli plague vaccine to Russian outbreak

tags: health
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Israeli researchers last year announced what the Jerusalem Post described as the world's first mRNA vaccine against a deadly bacterium, offering protection against pneumonic plague. The vaccine is not publicly available for human use. The timing was raised in connection with a current pneumonic plague situation in Russia.

Compilation of pandemic-era official statements presented as evidence of planning

tags: health, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

A montage of archived clips features health officials and public figures discussing preparations for a future pandemic, World Health Organization long-range planning, vaccine distribution strategy, media management during outbreaks, and lockdown rules on gatherings, shopping and funerals. The accompanying commentary characterizes these as a coordinated plan and calls for mass non-compliance.
